readings.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism.
readings.code_difference: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.

readings.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name.
readings.code_difference: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

readings.summary: Support formatter generation plus MessagePack metadata without a package reference by letting the generator and analyzers recognize user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes.
readings.code_difference: Rather than introducing a surrogate API, metadata discovery must accept matching user-declared attribute types in addition to the real MessagePack attributes, with corresponding analyzer and generator handling.

output.quote:
For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

readings.summary: Implement the core attributed partial-formatter generation feature, with contractless public-member serialization fallback and honoring any MessagePack attributes already present on T, but without adding the merely suggested surrogate-type API.
readings.code_difference: The generator implements IMessagePackFormatter<T> in the annotated bodyless partial class and adjusts member/key discovery for external T, while GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute needs no SurrogateType property or surrogate-based key mapping.

readings.summary: Implement the core formatter generation feature together with the suggested optional SurrogateType API so callers can supply MessagePack-attributed surrogate types whose property names determine keys and settings for Project A types.
readings.code_difference: In addition to generating the partial formatter, the public attribute exposes SurrogateType and the generator and relevant analyzers resolve and validate a surrogate, map its members to T by property name, and use its attributes instead of relying solely on T's contractless shape or own attributes.

vote.text: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings

A.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name.
A.code_difference: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

B.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism.
B.code_difference: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.

orientation.why: The attribute exposes `Type? SurrogateType`, and `GeneratedFormatterCollector` validates surrogate members and applies their `Key`/`IgnoreMember` annotations, with tests covering surrogate-controlled keys and membership.
